findings.title: Restore accepts snapshots larger than the configured capacity
findings.evidence: restore replaces entries without comparing snapshot.len() to capacity; put evicts only one entry before adding one (51-62).
findings.trigger: Restore a snapshot of three entries into a buffer of capacity two, then insert new keys.
findings.impact: The advertised bounded buffer remains oversized indefinitely; callers cannot rely on capacity as a memory bound.

findings.title: Zero-capacity KDA buffer still admits an entry
findings.evidence: At capacity zero evict_lfu returns on an empty map (67-68), then put inserts unconditionally (55-62).
findings.impact: len becomes one despite a zero capacity; disabling storage via a zero quota is ineffective.

findings.title: YouTube URL and output directory are interpolated into a shell
findings.evidence: run_cmd uses subprocess.run(shell=True) at line 9; URL is placed in double quotes at 17/36/42 and output_dir at 36.
findings.trigger: A supplied URL or output directory contains shell substitution such as $(command), or a quote that terminates the quoted argument.
findings.impact: Executing the acquisition script runs attacker-controlled shell commands with the operator account privileges.

findings.title: New face tracks are returned twice on their first frame
findings.evidence: New track is appended to assignments at 267-268 but never added to matched_tracks; the lost-track loop at 272-276 immediately increments lost and appends it again. c5_face_swap_cli.py:368-372 consumes update and :396 iterates every assignment.
findings.trigger: A detected face has no existing matching track and is assigned an identity with default max_extrapolate=2.
findings.impact: Face-swap processing runs twice for the same face on its initial frame, adds redundant inference/compositing, and incorrectly marks a new track as lost.

findings.title: Synthetic entropy demo presents label lookup as an empirical NLI comparison
findings.evidence: Clustering compares supplied semantic_id labels, probe weights are random (56-58), yet measurements are labeled Oxford NLI clustering (263) and SEP acceleration (347).
findings.trigger: Use run_empirical_stress_test output as comparative evidence about the cited semantic entropy or trained probe methods.
findings.impact: The reported speedup measures integer label grouping versus a random linear projection on fabricated activations, so it does not validate the referenced NLI/probe implementations.

findings.title: Unescaped description can break generated Python source
findings.evidence: contract.description is interpolated directly into a triple-double-quoted function docstring; McpCandidateContract is an unconstrained dataclass and deduce_contract accepts custom_description.
findings.trigger: A valid description includes a triple-double-quote sequence.
findings.impact: Scaffolding succeeds and persists a syntactically invalid server artifact; later initialization fails. No claim of execution-authorization bypass is made.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Creation fsyncs the file but no parent-directory fsync is visible in reviewed production lines 1-389; crash durability of a newly created pathname requires further platform/caller analysis.
hypotheses.status: not established as a defect in this audit
